message.reasoning:
The user wants to start Docker on Windows using docker start. They likely want to run a command to start Docker service. On Windows, Docker Desktop runs as a service. The command "docker start" is used to start containers, not the Docker daemon. To start Docker Desktop, you might need to start the Docker Desktop application or the Docker service. The user says "start Docker on window using docker start." That might be a misunderstanding. We can explain that docker start starts containers, not the Docker engine. To start Docker engine, you need to start Docker Desktop or the Docker service. On Windows, you can use "net start com.docker.service" or "Start-Service Docker" in PowerShell. Or you can run "docker-machine start default" if using Docker Machine. But likely they want to start Docker Desktop. We can provide a command to start the Docker service via PowerShell: "Start-Service com.docker.service". Or via cmd: "net start com.docker.service". Or if using Docker Desktop, you can start the application.

We can also mention that if Docker Desktop is installed, you can start it by launching the Docker Desktop app. If you want to start the Docker daemon from command line, you can use "dockerd" but that requires admin privileges.

We can provide a script to start Docker Desktop via command line: "C:\Program Files\Docker\Docker\Docker Desktop.exe". Or use "Start-Process -FilePath 'C:\Program Files\Docker\Docker\Docker Desktop.exe'".

But the user specifically says "start Docker on window using docker start." So we can respond that docker start is for containers, not for starting Docker itself. Provide correct commands.
